question: Which of the following Union Territories has the lowest population as per the Census of India 2011?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lakshadweep**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lakshadweep** has the lowest population among all Union Territories in India as per the Census of 2011.
 
• The population of Lakshadweep is approximately **64,429** according to the 2011 Census.
 
• Lakshadweep is an archipelago consisting of 36 islands, located in the Arabian Sea.
 
• Despite its small population, Lakshadweep has a high literacy rate of around 92.28%.
 
• The economy of Lakshadweep is primarily dependent on fisheries and tourism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census of India 2011**

 
 
• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• The 2011 Census was the 15th National Census of the country.
 
• It provides comprehensive data on the population, including demographic, economic, and social data.
 
• The 2011 Census revealed that India's total population was approximately 1.21 billion.
 
 
 
• **Union Territories of India**
 
 
• India has a total of 8 Union Territories as of the latest administrative reorganization.
 
• Union Territories are regions that are directly governed by the Central Government of India.
 
• Some other Union Territories include Delhi, Chandigarh, and Puducherry.
 
 
 
• **Demographic Data**
 
 
• Demographic data includes information on population size, density, distribution, and composition.
 
• It is crucial for planning and implementing government policies and programs.
 
• Accurate demographic data helps in addressing various socio-economic issues and resource allocation.
 
 
 
• **Fisheries in Lakshadweep**
 
 
• The waters around Lakshadweep are rich in marine life, making fisheries a major economic activity.
 
• The main catches include tuna, shark, and various other fish species.
 
• Fishing techniques are traditional and sustainable, preserving the marine ecosystem.
